title: Finite-open pairs satisfy fppf descent
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention], and let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism of $S$-schemes. On $S$-schemes let $P_f(T)$ be the set of pairs $(a,Z)$ with $a:T\to Y$ an $S$-map and $Z\subseteq X\times_{Y,a}T$ an open subscheme [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-open-immersion] finite over $T$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], with restriction by pullback. Then $P_f$ is a sheaf of sets for the big fppf topology [def-pc-fppf-site]. Explicitly, for every fppf covering family $\{T_i\to T\}$ and pairs $(a_i,Z_i)$ whose pullbacks agree on every $T_i\times_TT_j$, there is a unique pair $(a,Z)\in P_f(T)$ pulling back to all $(a_i,Z_i)$. No separatedness, finite type, flatness, or finite presentation assumption on $f$ is required.

source.place: Tag 04PE (lemma-finite-sheaf), part (1), restricted to scheme source and target.

proof.text: First check restriction. For $h:T^{\prime}\to T$, write $W=X\times_{Y,a}T$ and $W^{\prime}=X\times_{Y,ah}T^{\prime}$. The universal property of fibre products identifies $W^{\prime}$ with $W\times_TT^{\prime}$, compatibly with both projections. The inverse image of the open $Z\subset W$ is the open subscheme on that inverse-image open set; it represents $Z\times_TT^{\prime}$, since a map to $W^{\prime}$ factors through it exactly when its composite to $W$ factors through $Z$. Its projection to $T^{\prime}$ is finite by base-change stability of finite morphisms in [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange]. Inverse images compose and preserve identities, so these restrictions define $P_f$ as a presheaf.

source.place: Tag 04PE (lemma-finite-sheaf), proof of part (1), first paragraph, specialized to schemes.

proof.text: Let $\{v_i:T_i\to T\}$ be an fppf cover and $(a_i,Z_i)$ a matching family. By [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc] this is an fpqc cover. Equality of pairs on overlaps implies $a_i\operatorname{pr}_1=a_j\operatorname{pr}_2$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] with target $Y$ to obtain the unique scheme map $a:T\to Y$ restricting to $a_i$. It is an $S$-map: its composite to $S$ and the given structure map of $T$ have equal restrictions on all $T_i$, hence are equal by the uniqueness clause of that same node with target $S$.

source.place: Tag 04PE (lemma-finite-sheaf), proof of part (1), first paragraph, specialized to schemes.

proof.text: Put $W=X\times_{Y,a}T$ and $W_i=W\times_TT_i$. The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $W_i$ with $X\times_{Y,a_i}T_i$, and $W_i\times_WW_j$ with $X\times_Y(T_i\times_TT_j)$: each identification is the unique map preserving the $X,T_i,T_j$ projections, and its inverse is given by the same projections. Thus the matching condition on the $Z_i$ is equality of their inverse-image opens on $W_i\times_WW_j$. By [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change] the family $\{W_i\to W\}$ is fppf, hence fpqc by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-subscheme-fpqc-descent] to this cover and these opens. It gives a unique open subscheme $Z\subset W$ whose pullback to $W_i$ is $Z_i$.

source.place: Tag 04PE (lemma-finite-sheaf), proof of part (1), first paragraph, specialized to schemes.

proof.text: For the projection $p:Z\to T$, its base change to $T_i$ is $Z\times_TT_i\to T_i$. Under the fibre-product identifications of step 3 and the open-subscheme identification there, this is exactly the given finite morphism $Z_i\to T_i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-finite] along the fpqc cover $\{T_i\to T\}$ from step 2. Hence $p$ is finite, so $(a,Z)\in P_f(T)$ and its restrictions are all the prescribed pairs.

source.place: Tag 04PE (lemma-finite-sheaf), proof of part (1), first paragraph, specialized to schemes.

proof.text: If another pair $(b,Z^{\prime})$ has those restrictions, uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] gives $b=a$. Regard both open subschemes as opens in the same $W=X\times_{Y,a}T$. Their restrictions to each $W_i$ equal $Z_i$, so uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-open-subscheme-fpqc-descent] gives $Z^{\prime}=Z$. This is uniqueness of the pair, and establishes the sheaf condition for every fppf covering. Only properties of the covering and the local finite projections were used; no hypothesis on $f$ has been introduced.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q15-f318a3d44 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full: 5 steps and no new nodes. Its statement matches Stacks 04PE (lemma-finite-sheaf) part (1) in spaces-more-groupoids.tex, specialized to schemes: no hypothesis on f, and pairs (a,Z) with Z open in X×_{Y,a}T and finite over T. I compared each step with the first paragraph of the Stacks proof. Step 1: the presheaf structure follows from the fibre-product universal property and finite base change (lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange, a Mathlib leaf). Step 2: a is obtained by fpqc representable descent with target Y; its uniqueness with target S makes a an S-map. Step 3: the identifications W_i=X×_{Y,a_i}T_i and W_i×_W W_j=X×_Y(T_ij) are correct. The cover {W_i→W} is fppf by base change and therefore fpqc, so 03N0 open descent applies. Step 4: Z×_T T_i is Z_i, and 02LA finiteness descent applies along the fpqc cover. Step 5: uniqueness follows from both uniqueness clauses. Edge cases I checked: empty base, empty cover and empty X; non-quasi-compact T, handled by the fpqc family notion; non-separated f. The only citer, lem-sfb-unmarked-finite-open-parts-space, uses exactly this sheaf property. There are no duplicates (rg over 04PE and finite-open nodes) and no cycle. Batch-5 check: lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc (022C) and lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change (021O(3)) are Mathlib leaves stating general facts about fppf covering families. Neither is part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, and they are the only trf or Poincaré-duality nodes in the proof closure, so I accept them. I accept both tool_uses (pbc 03N0 and 02LA, generic scheme descent).
